data.cultural_impact: The name Mutalib holds a significant cultural impact in the Muslim world, particularly in the Arabic-speaking countries. As it is derived from Arabic, Mutalib is considered a unique and classic Arabic name. It is often given to boys as a Badr (good) name (a name given to a boy that is pleasing and auspicious). In some cultures within the Muslim world, the name Mutalib may be used as a sign of respect or attachment to the Prophet Ibrahim (AS), due to the biblical association of the name with the late-stage fatherhood of the Prophet Ibrahim (AS).
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mutalib carries a deep spiritual significance for Muslims as it is associated with the Prophet Ibrahim (AS), who is held in high regard within the faith. The name represents a person who is wholly dedicated and devout to Allah and His guidance in life. It is a reminder that no matter what stage of life we are in, it is never too late to turn towards the Creator with sincere intentions and seek His pleasure. Furthermore, the name Mutalib is a promise of a blessed family and a reminder of the prophetic story of Ibrahim (AS) who received his son, Ishmael (AS), in his old age after his repeated prayers to Allah.

historical_references.reference: Mutalib was the name of the Meccan idol merchant to whom the Prophet Muhammad was entrusted as an infant.
historical_references.context: Mutalib was a caretaker, providing for the young Muhammad when his parents died, and helped ensure his survival during his formative years.

historical_references.reference: Mutalib is also the name of the great-grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad, who provided shelter to the Prophet's grandfather, Abdullah, and his tribe, the Hashim, in the pre-Islamic era (around 500 CE).
historical_references.context: Mutalib's hospitality and support for Abdullah and the Hashim tribe helped establish a tradition of generosity and protection among their descendants, including the Prophet Muhammad himself.
